notes:
Remote ID no longer loses the operator's location before the first arm.

The operator location was the spot the aircraft lifted off from, which
is only recorded at the moment the motors start. Before the first
takeoff of a session there was no such spot, so the controller's own
GPS stood in — and with no fix on the controller, nothing was sent at
all and the autopilot reported the operator location lost. That landed
at pre-arm, holding up the very launch it was waiting on.

A disarmed aircraft is already standing where it will lift off from, so
its own position now answers for the operator location until it flies.
Its receiver is the better of the two, and it cannot arm without a fix.
Once it is airborne, the controller's position stands in as before.
